extracted.intended_audience: public company executives, CFOs, investor relations officers (IROs), and corporate securities counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for public companies on disclosure practices covering non-GAAP financial measures, Regulation FD (selective disclosure), and Regulation M-A (M&A communications), including what must be disclosed, how, and timing/format requirements. Intended to help issuers adopt compliant investor-relations policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory disclosure triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists circumstances that create mandatory disclosure obligations under the 1933 and 1934 Acts, SEC rules and stock exchange rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory disclosures include: any 1933 Act registration statement (e.g., IPO prospectus on Form S-1, later Form S-3); every 1934 Act annual or quarterly report (Form 10-K or 10-Q); any event requiring a Form 8-K; when the company is “in the marketplace” to buy or sell its stock (the “disclose or abstain” rule); when confirming or correcting a rumor that began with company-leaked information causing unusual trading activity; when required by stock exchange requirements; and to update prior statements the market considers current or “evergreen.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary disclosure governed by key SEC rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Three key SEC regimes guide voluntary disclosures: Regulation G (GAAP/non-GAAP), Item 10(e) of Regulation S‑K (filed non‑GAAP disclosures), and Regulation FD (fair disclosure). Regulation M‑A governs transactional/merger communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making voluntary disclosures (earnings calls, analyst meetings, web/social posts), follow the guardrails of these rules and related SEC C&DIs; remember Regulation G/Item 10(e) and C&DIs cover non-GAAP measures, Regulation FD covers selective disclosure, and Regulation M‑A covers M&A written communications and filing on date of first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of non‑GAAP financial measures (Regulation G / Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non‑GAAP financial measures are numerical measures of historical or future performance, financial position or cash flow created by adjusting a comparable GAAP measure (generally by eliminating or including specific metrics). KPIs calculated on a non‑GAAP basis are treated as non‑GAAP measures. Metrics based only on operating/statistical data (e.g., same‑store sales, number of employees) are not non‑GAAP; ratios using only GAAP measures are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware SEC treats many common metrics (adjusted EBITDA, adjusted free cash flow, net debt) as non‑GAAP and scrutinizes them via comment letters and enforcement actions. Clarify whether a metric is non‑GAAP before public use.

rubrics_metrics.name: KPI disclosure guidelines for MD&A
rubrics_metrics.description: When including KPIs/operating metrics in MD&A, disclose these four items even if the KPI is not a non‑GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Provide a clear definition of the metric and how it is calculated; (2) Include a statement why the metric is useful to investors and how management uses it; (3) Consider whether estimates/assumptions underlying the metric need disclosure to avoid misleading investors; (4) Consider whether presentation or calculation differences from prior years need explanation or recasting of prior metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile non‑GAAP measures to the most directly comparable GAAP measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any public release of material information that contains a non‑GAAP financial measure must present the most directly comparable GAAP information and a reconciliation of the non‑GAAP measure to that GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all public communications (written, oral, web, social, webcasts). For oral disclosures, companies may post the reconciliation on their website and provide the website address during the presentation. Present non‑GAAP consistently across disclosures and be cautious about measures you cannot justify including in filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence requirement under Item 10(e) of Regulation S‑K
rubrics_metrics.description: For SEC‑filed disclosures containing non‑GAAP measures, companies must present the comparable GAAP financial measure with prominence equal to or greater than the non‑GAAP measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: earnings release headers that include a non‑GAAP number should also contain the comparable GAAP number. Item 10(e) imposes stricter rules for filed (as opposed to furnished) information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management explanation for non‑GAAP usefulness (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Management must disclose the reasons it believes the non‑GAAP measure is useful and, to the extent material, any additional purposes for its use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation should be substantive — state why the measure helps investors and how management uses it; avoid boilerplate or vague rationales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on certain liquidity measures (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than EBIT or EBITDA, companies should not present liquidity measures that exclude charges or liabilities requiring cash settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EBIT and EBITDA are acceptable, but stripping out cash‑settling liabilities from liquidity metrics (other than these) is discouraged/prohibited under Item 10(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on 'smoothing' non‑GAAP performance measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should not adjust non‑GAAP performance measures to smooth or eliminate items labelled nonrecurring/infrequent/unusual if such items are reasonably likely to recur within two years or a similar charge/gain occurred in the prior two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments within the two‑year window may be made only if not described as nonrecurring/infrequent/unusual. Avoid using adjustments to disguise recurring costs or to create a misleading trend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not present non‑GAAP measures on the face of financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should not present non‑GAAP financial measures on the face of financial statements, notes to financial statements, or pro forma financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep non‑GAAP measures separate from audited financial statements and footnotes to avoid implying they are GAAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confusingly similar titles for non‑GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should use titles/descriptions for non‑GAAP measures clearly different from GAAP captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use labels that could be mistaken for GAAP metrics; choose clear, descriptive names to avoid investor confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid misleading adjustments and presentations for non‑GAAP measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must avoid adjustments that make non‑GAAP numbers misleading, including excluding normal recurring cash operating expenses or selectively excluding nonrecurring charges while keeping gains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti‑patterns to avoid: misleading adjustments; inconsistent presentation across periods; selective exclusions of charges but not gains; individually tailored metrics that substitute for GAAP recognition methods. These practices invite SEC scrutiny and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD: requirement to publicly disclose selective voluntary disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a company or someone acting on its behalf voluntarily discloses material nonpublic information to securities market professionals or certain security holders where trading is reasonably foreseeable, the company must inform the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure was intentional, public disclosure must be simultaneous (in practice often prior to limited audience). If unintentional, the company must make public disclosure promptly: by the later of 24 hours after the unintentional disclosure or before the next trading day's open if more than 24 hours away. The SEC’s 24‑hour clock starts when a senior official learns of and recognizes the disclosed information as material and nonpublic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing unintentional disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: When an inadvertent selective disclosure occurs, promptly distribute the material nonpublic information to the public via press release, website, social media or Form 8‑K (Item 7.01) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 7.01 may be used as a "super‑press release" to furnish (not file) the curative disclosure. Practical guidance: if you suspect a mistake, pause, consult IRO/general counsel, correct the statement, then distribute the material information by press release, Form 8‑K, or both on the same day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical tip: follow a script at conferences to avoid inadvertent disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Unscripted Q&A at conferences may create inadvertent disclosures of material nonpublic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before presenting, disclose in a press release or Form 8‑K the material information you want to be free to discuss; pre‑announce and arrange a webcast; have IRO or CFO listen and help the presenter decline to answer unscripted questions that would require disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies communications exempt from Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions include: discussions with persons who expressly agree to maintain confidentiality (written or verbal NDAs required to be more than implicit); ordinary course business disclosure to customers/suppliers; disclosure by foreign private issuers (subject to Chapter 15 qualifications); disclosure to persons who owe a duty of trust or confidence (lawyers, bankers, financial advisors, accountants); many 1933 Act registered offering communications (e.g., road shows) though some registrations (Form S‑8, Form S‑3 resale) remain subject to FD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website and social media can satisfy Regulation FD if certain tests met
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting material information on a company website or social media can be public disclosure for Reg FD if the outlet is a recognized distribution channel and disseminates broadly with time for absorption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three SEC tests: (1) Recognized channel for distribution — steps taken to alert market to use of site/social for disclosures; (2) Broad dissemination — is posting accessible to securities marketplace generally; (3) Time to absorb — did posting give investors enough time to absorb/react (depends on company size, steps to alert investors, nature/complexity). Recommend include cautionary legend in Form 10‑K/10‑Q describing intent to use website/social channels and which channels will be used. Caution: personal posts by officers may violate FD if channels not recognized; example: DraftKings CEO post led to SEC action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation FD liability contours
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD is not an antifraud rule; liability is limited and SEC monitors conduct actively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuer liability under Reg FD requires knowing or reckless conduct (not good faith mistakes in materiality judgments). Reg FD creates no private right of action. Other antifraud liabilities (e.g., Rule 10b‑5, duty‑to‑correct/update theories) remain available against issuers for selective disclosure or failures to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard and hot buttons
rubrics_metrics.description: Materiality follows Supreme Court/SEC guidance: information is material if a reasonable shareholder would consider it important or it would have significantly altered the total mix of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No bright‑line tests; balance probability and magnitude for contingent events. SEC 'hot buttons' companies should review for materiality: earnings information; mergers/acquisitions/tender offers/joint ventures; new products/customers/suppliers developments; changes of control or senior management; auditor changes; events regarding securities (defaults, splits, dividend changes, offerings); bankruptcy/receivership. SAB 99 warns against mechanical % thresholds; qualitative factors may render small amounts material (examples listed in SAB 99 such as masking a change in earnings, hiding failure to meet consensus, affecting compensation triggers, etc.). Use percentage rules of thumb (e.g., 5%) only cautiously as a starting point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical checklist for earnings call compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended pre/during/post steps to ensure earnings calls comply with Regulation FD and non‑GAAP disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before call: issue press release or broadly disseminated web/social notice several days/weeks ahead with time/date/access and state discussion may cover material developments; pre‑release earnings results by press release/web disclosure and furnish to SEC under Item 2.02 of Form 8‑K; post all financial/statistical data and required non‑GAAP reconciliations on website before the call. During: hold the call within 48 hours after Form 8‑K filing. After: if call contains new material nonpublic information and occurs >48 hours after Form 8‑K, furnish transcript within four business days; post audio/transcript promptly and provide access for at least one year and archive with disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation M‑A filing requirement for M&A communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must file with the SEC any written communication made in connection with or relating to a business combination transaction that is provided to the public or persons not parties to the transaction, starting from the first public announcement until the transaction closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Regulation M‑A written communication must include a prominently displayed legend directing investors to read the relevant registration/proxy/tender documents and to the SEC site. Exclusions: factual business information solely about ordinary business matters; internal communications provided solely to parties to the transaction; oral communications (but posted audio/video/slides require filing a transcript). File communications on or before the 'date of first use.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay between Regulation M‑A and non‑GAAP rules (Reg G / Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial forecasts used by advisors in M&A contexts may be excluded from Regulation G/Item 10(e) if certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecasts do not trigger Reg G/Item 10(e) (and need not be reconciled) so long as: they are used by the financial advisor to render an opinion materially related to the transaction, and they are disclosed to comply with M‑A requirements. However, if the same non‑GAAP measures appear in a registration statement or proxy statement, Reg G/Item 10(e) will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay between Regulation M‑A and Regulation FD (format vs timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: When both Regulations M‑A and FD apply to a communication, different aspects govern compliance: format obligations come from M‑A, timing obligations from FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a format that satisfies Regulation M‑A (e.g., include legend and file as required), but for timing, comply with Regulation FD by making prior or simultaneous public disclosure (i.e., FD's timing rules govern).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate spokespeople and approval procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure policy should specify procedures for drafting, reviewing, approving and distributing all material communications and identify authorized spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which individuals (chair, CEO, CFO, IRO, etc.) may speak to analysts and investors. Ensure review/approval workflows and counsel oversight to avoid inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality determination process
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a process (with company counsel as necessary) to determine whether information is material and whether it needs disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and follow the process; involve counsel and relevant committees (Disclosure Practices Committee, Audit Committee, managers) when appropriate. Adhere to policies rather than ad‑hoc judgments to reduce hindsight risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and prominence of cautionary language for forward‑looking statements
rubrics_metrics.description: All oral and written communications should include legends or meaningful cautionary language for forward‑looking statements to fall within statutory safe harbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written forward‑looking statements must include meaningful cautionary language identifying the statements and the important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially; boilerplate is insufficient. For oral forward‑looking statements, provide a declaration pointing to a readily available written document (e.g., recent Form 10‑K/10‑Q) with factors; tailor and make warnings conspicuous. Regularly update risk factors to reflect current risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: One‑on‑one analyst/investor meetings policy (timing and subject matter limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt rules limiting one‑on‑one contacts to avoid selective disclosure and comply with FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: limit one‑on‑one conversations to the period following an earnings call until a blackout period. Subject matter: prepare scripts/responses to anticipated questions and limit responses to elaboration of previously disclosed or generally known information. Do not comment on or confirm previous earnings guidance or individual analyst projections; address consensus only carefully. Avoid responding to questions about potential financings, restructurings, acquisitions, mergers, or unusual market activity unless required by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat media interviews as if subject to Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications with news media should be treated the same as communications to market professionals under Reg FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume media interviews can create selective disclosure obligations — prepare scripts, clearances and cautionary language accordingly; do not rely on informal or off‑the‑record assumptions to avoid FD obligations.
